dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Is this the legendary Serenitea Pot? I've read about it, but I never imagined the inside would look like this...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: And it's not just the Serenitea Pot, I've read about loads of other artifacts and mechanisms, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me, I'm not a child anymore. Moving to a new environment isn't going to throw me out of whack.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Even when I was traveling with the caravan and living life on the road, I never had any difficulty adapting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That reminds me, whereabouts in Mondstadt do you live, Prune?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I'm staying with a relative. She's my grandfather's cousin's son's...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Uhm, you know what? The details aren't important. The point is, we're related.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: But because Mom and Dad sent them a letter saying to "keep a close eye on me," they've given me a curfew at night... Honestly, it's not like SHE'S my mom...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you allowed to be here?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Oh, it's fine. I already told her I was coming.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Which reminds me, are there any rules I need to abide by? Curfews, off-limit areas, things I shouldn't touch...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: None at all. Only adults come up with rules like that.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Really!? Oh, that's amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: This is such a great vacation spot. Everyone must love your home!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: And I do, too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to chat?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Since you asked, I'd quite like to talk about my arch nemesis, Alice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I consider you both friends...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I'm not asking you to take sides. Witches have all sorts of tricks up their sleeves to beguile and ensnare the unwary, so I don't blame you for falling under her spell.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: But you're smart, so I trust your judgment. Before long, the spell will fade, and you'll see her for who she really is!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: What I really wanted to say is that lately I've been wondering... Why is it that every time I think I've won, things always just seem to end up going the way she planned?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Ugh, it's so frustrating! I need someone who understands witches to help me work it out...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: What's the logic behind Alice's schemes?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: C'mon, you're smart. Help me figure out a way to turn the tables. I wanna give her a taste of what it's like to miscalculate for once!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you considered that maybe Alice's schemes don't follow any normal logic?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: That's it! That wicked witch does whatever she wants! Acting without regard for others in pursuit of her own ideas of fun!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: So then, what's the best way to deal with her?

choices.text: Throw a tantrum and roll around on the floor...?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Why would I do that? Screaming and shouting and annoying everyone nearby... People would hate me.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Wait a second... Something's wrong here. You're not the Traveler at all, are you? You're a witch in disguise!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Reveal yourself! I know it's you!

choices.text: What I was trying to say is... Stop overthinking everything.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Hmm... I don't think that's something I can do so easily...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: But I can try to learn a thing or two from Klee and the others...

choices.text: Why not let yourself be a child for once and do whatever you want?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I'm glad you asked. I've decided to take your advice — I'm going to conduct an experiment!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: It's just a trial run, really... I'm going to try being a carefree, regular child for a day.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: A whole day!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess you have to start somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I even did a "warm-up" last night in preparation.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I closed all my books, put away my stationery, and kept reminding myself that there's no need to arrive at any conclusions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And then...?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Well, I was thinking about this as I lay in bed. What would a regular kid be doing right now? Listening to a story? Drawing? Drinking some warm milk before bed? Or maybe they'd already be asleep!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I stayed up so late thinking about it that this morning, I almost missed the optimal time to wake up naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're still overthinking things...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Mhm... I realized that, too. So, to remove all thought from the equation, I decided to make a "To-Do List for Kids."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So what's on your list?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Item one: toss and turn in bed (immediately after waking up). Then, get told to get up (do not get out of bed unprompted). Since there's no one to prompt me, I just pretend to be someone else and tell myself to get up.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: It isn't ideal, but I've decided it counts.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Item two: be a fussy eater. I tried to find something to complain about, but I just couldn't bring myself to see it through.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: That's why I've written "item failed" on the list.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Item three: snack uncontrollably. This one was the easiest, and my favorite.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: ...But halfway through, I realized I'd made a mistake.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: In the real world, no adult would ever actually let their child eat as much junk food as they wanted.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Item three: play meaningless games. This one was hard!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I ended up focusing all my attention on trying to find loopholes in the rules...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like things didn't go to plan...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Correct. So now I'm going to throw a tantrum!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I'm going to put away my to-do list and declare my experiment a huge failure! Then, I'm not going to make any effort whatsoever to learn from my mistakes!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I don't want to reflect on why I failed, and I don't want to listen to reason. I... just... don't... care!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is "throwing a tantrum" also on your list?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Eh!? How did you know?

choices.text: Because children are allowed to be unreasonable. It's in the job description.
So maybe your experiment was successful after all!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Prune.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Good morning. Are you going outside today?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: My advice is to do the hardest chores first. If you put them off till evening, you won't be in the mood to get them done at all...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Prune.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Is it that late already? Even the clearest minds need rest. Good night.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: You should get some shut-eye, too. I know how grown-ups like to stay up late overthinking things.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Hmm... I like the way you've decorated this place. Very professional.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: This desk is big enough to have three books open at once. But that bookshelf is so tall...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Never mind, I can see a stool. I'll just climb on that.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: When I lived in Nasha Town, I liked to find cozy corners to nestle into so I could read my books while watching people come and go.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I realized that the rules written in books never change, but people are always breaking them anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: You've been very faithful to the original style — this room reminds me of all sorts of weird and wonderful stories. If you have the time, maybe I can share some of them with you?
